title: णत्वप्रकरणम् — The Natva (Retroflex ण) Rule Book
subtitle: Compiled from two independent classroom source documents on णत्वम् (the ऋ/र्/ष्-triggered retroflexion of न् to ण्), cross-referenced to Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī where citations are given in the source materials
source_note: This rulebook merges two source PDFs on the same topic (natva): '10_णत्वप्रकरणम् (काव्यदपठनार्थम्)' and '10_णत्वम्'. Both cover the same core rule (रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे) but were evidently produced by different instructors/compilers, since they cite DIFFERENT sūtra numbers for the same rule: the first cites 8.4.1 (which matches the standard, widely-attested Aṣṭādhyāyī numbering for this sūtra), while the second cites 8.4.41. This is flagged as an unresolved discrepancy between the two source documents rather than silently resolved -- 8.4.1 is used as the primary ashtadhyayi_ref since it matches standard reference numbering, with the alternate citation preserved in a note. All other sūtra citations in this file are taken directly from whichever source PDF stated them, without independent re-verification beyond this one flagged case.

how_to_read.ashtadhyayi_ref: Chapter.Pada.Sutra number in Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī, as cited in the source material
how_to_read.nimitta: निमित्तम् -- the phonetic trigger/cause for the rule

rvowel_context.english_name: Core rule: ऋ/र्/ष् trigger retroflexion of a following न् to ण्
rvowel_context.rule: Within a single unsegmented word (समानपदे), when a following न् is preceded -- without any intervening word-boundary -- by ऋ, र्, or ष्, that न् is replaced by ण्. This is the foundational natva rule; all following entries describe how far this triggering reaches and where it is blocked.
related_ashtadhyayi: 8.4.41 (alternate citation given in one source document for the same rule -- see source_note)
rvowel_context.book_ref: 10_णत्वप्रकरणम् and 10_णत्वम् (both source PDFs; both give this as the opening/core rule)
rvowel_context.process: आदेशः (substitution): निमित्तं (ऋ/र्/ष्) + न् → ण्, within one अखण्डपद

examples.gloss: ऋ-triggered (attributed to the extension ऋणृतो नस्य णत्वं वाच्यम्, see natva-2)

rvowel_context.english_name: Extension: ऋ itself (not just र्/ष्) independently triggers natva
rvowel_context.rule: A separate statement (वार्तिक-प्रकृति) clarifies that ऋ, on its own, also counts as a natva trigger for a following न् -- not only र् and ष्. This is why root-vowel ऋ (as in विसृ, पितृ) triggers the change even though it is a vowel, not the consonants र्/ष्.
rvowel_context.process: वार्तिकः (supplementary clarifying statement) extending the trigger-set of natva-1 to include ऋ itself

rvowel_context.english_name: Natva reaches across an intervening अट्/कवर्ग/पवर्ग/आङ्/अनुस्वार, not just directly-adjacent न्
rvowel_context.rule: The trigger (ऋ/र्/ष्) need not be immediately adjacent to the न् -- natva still applies even if any of the following intervene between them: a vowel or the semivowels ह्/य्/व्/र् (जोड़ी named अट् here), a velar consonant (कवर्ग: क्/ख्/ग्/घ्/ङ्), a labial consonant (पवर्ग: प्/फ्/ब्/भ्/म्), the prefix आ (आङ्), or an anusvāra (नुम्).
rvowel_context.process: आदेशः, with the trigger's reach extended across specific intervening sound-classes (व्यवधानम्)
rvowel_context.flagged_nuance: The 'अट्' referenced here is a technical pratyāhāra covering vowels plus ह्/य्/व्/र् -- not the augment 'अट्' (used in the imperfect/aorist) of the same name. Both source PDFs also reproduce the full Māheśvara-sūtra (शिवसूत्र) list to define exactly which sounds belong to each of the referenced classes (कवर्ग, पवर्ग, etc.) -- reproduced in natva-4 below as reference material rather than as a separate operative rule.

examples.gloss: पवर्ग (प्) intervenes between ष् and न्

rvowel_context.english_name: Reference table: the sound-groups (अट्/कवर्ग/पवर्ग etc.) that may intervene without blocking natva
rvowel_context.rule: Both source documents reproduce the fourteen Māheśvara-sūtras (शिवसूत्राणि) -- Pāṇini's foundational phoneme-groupings -- to precisely define which sounds fall under अट्, कवर्ग, and पवर्ग for the purposes of natva-3. This entry is reference material, not an independently operative rule.
rvowel_context.sutra_devanagari: अइउण् ऋऌक् एओङ् ऐऔच् हयवरट् लण् ञमङणनम् झभञ् घढधष् जबगडदश् खफछठथचटतव् कपय् शषसर् हल्
rvowel_context.process: reference/definitional (शिवसूत्राणि), not itself a substitution rule

rvowel_context.english_name: In compounds, natva is obligatory when the result is a proper name (संज्ञा)
rvowel_context.rule: When the compound (समस्तपद) as a whole functions as a fixed name (संज्ञा), natva of the uttarapada's initial न् is obligatory (नित्यम्), not merely optional as in the general compound case (see natva-6).
rvowel_context.process: पूर्वपदस्थ निमित्तात् उत्तरपदस्थ नकारस्य णकारः नित्यं भवति संज्ञायां

rvowel_context.english_name: In ordinary (non-name) compounds, natva of the second member is optional
rvowel_context.rule: Prāt‍ipadika-final न् (or a न् governed by विभक्ति or अनुस्वार-context) in the uttarapada of a compound optionally (विकल्पेन) takes natva when the pūrvapada carries the trigger -- both the retroflexed and plain-dental forms are valid.
rvowel_context.process: विकल्पेन आदेशः -- both forms are grammatically acceptable in a general (non-saṃjñā) compound

examples.sandhi: माष + वापा + न् + इ = माषवापाणि / माषवापानि

examples.gloss: कवर्ग-व्यवधान compound, natva नित्यं here per the source (contrast with the general optional case)

rvowel_context.english_name: Prohibition: natva never applies to a word-final न्
rvowel_context.rule: Even if the retroflexion-trigger (ऋ/र्/ष्) is present earlier in the same word, a न् standing at the absolute end of the word (पदान्त) never undergoes natva.
rvowel_context.process: निषेधः (blocking rule) -- overrides natva-1 specifically at word-final position

examples.gloss: word-final न्, natva blocked despite the र् earlier in राम

rvowel_context.english_name: Prohibition: natva is blocked if a sound outside the permitted intervening set (natva-3/natva-4) comes between the trigger and न्
rvowel_context.rule: If, within a single word, any sound OTHER than अट्/कवर्ग/पवर्ग/आङ्/अनुस्वार stands between the ऋ/र्/ष् trigger and the following न्, natva does not apply -- the न् remains dental.
rvowel_context.process: निषेधः -- a direct converse-application of natva-3's permitted-intervener list

examples.gloss: श् intervenes (not in the permitted set) -- natva blocked

summary_counts.status: Covers both source PDFs on natva in full. This is a narrower, single-topic rulebook (unlike the sandhi/samasa rulebooks) since both sources treat only this one sandhi phenomenon.
